abstract: Short QT Syndrome (SQTS) is a rare cardiac channelopathy characterized by abnormally short QTc intervals and increased sudden cardiac death (SCD) risk. Only 20-30% of SQTS cases have been linked to genetic mutations, typi-cally in surface membrane ion channels. We identified a novel lysosomal TMEM175 gene mutation (p.Arg377His) in 7 patients in a family with SQTS and SCD. Genetic analyses, including whole exome sequencing in the family and rare-variant burden testing in [~]118,000 UK Biobank participants, sug-gested an association between TMEM175 rare variants and QT interval short-ening. Functional studies in CRISPR-engineered mice and patient-specific induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes (iPSC-CMs) revealed that TMEM175R377H causes shortened QT intervals and hastened repolariza-tion, respectively, as well an increased arrhythmia susceptibility. Isolated TMEM175R377H cardiomyocytes showed action potential duration (APD) abbre-viation, confirmed in whole TMEM175R377H mouse hearts and patient-specific iPSC-CM monolayers. In silico and electron microscopy studies showed that TMEM175R377H disrupts lysosomal-mitochondrial interactions, leading to mito-chondrial dysfunction, as evidenced by the reduced maximal respiration and spare respiratory capacity, with reduced ATP production, IKATP activation, and APD shortening. This mutation represents the first non-sarcolemmal ion chan-nel defect associated with SQTS and high SCD risk, potentially expanding the genetic landscape of the disease.
